What a home means

A home is more than walls

A home is where a child feels safe.

It is the roof that shelters them from rain and heat.

It is where the family returns after a long day.

It is where an orphan should find peace, not fear of a crumbling roof or a cracked wall.

That is why renovating an orphan family's home is not just repairing a house…

It is restoring a space where people live with dignity.

And your gift can be part of that safety.

The work you support

Why renovation?

Because safety begins at home

Bahjah began maintaining and renovating orphans' homes after Cyclone Mekunu in 2018, when a specialist team visited homes, recorded cases and assessed the maintenance and renovation needed.

Since then, maintenance and renovation work has continued throughout the year, and its pace increases when Oman is affected by severe weather.

Every home has its need. Every family has its story. And every gift can change something important in a family's life.

Renovating the homes of orphans and widows is not just repairing "concrete"; it is security for their hearts.From Bahjah's announcement of the campaign to renovate 10 homes of widows and orphans, March 2026 (translated from Arabic)

Source: Bahjah's official profile (maintenance and renovation) and the official campaign announcement

From Bahjah's work

The 10-homes campaign… a legacy of Ramadan

During Ramadan, in March 2026, Bahjah launched a campaign to renovate ten homes of orphan and widow families.

The campaign included work such as:

  • Repairing deteriorated roofs
  • Restoring cracked walls
  • Preparing kitchens, bathrooms and essential facilities

The need for renovation may continue after the campaign, so the "Building & Renovation" fund remains open for cases that need support.

Source (archived copy of Bahjah's website)

  • Since 2018

    Maintaining homes in Wilayat Mirbat

    Bahjah implemented the Minister of Social Development's recommendation to maintain 5 homes in Wilayat Mirbat, as part of the maintenance and renovation work that began after Cyclone Mekunu.

  • A Bahjah project

    Bahjah Residential Complex

    A residential and commercial complex that provides housing for orphans, made up of four buildings with a garden and outdoor spaces.

    Source (archived copy of Bahjah's website)

  • Goal: 2040

    Charity Buildings Administration

    Bahjah aims to complete 10 charitable buildings by 2040 to ensure a sustainable income, and has completed the first building, thank God.

    Source (archived copy of Bahjah's website)

Why Bahjah?

When you give… you deserve peace of mind

The Omani Bahjah Orphan Society is a non-governmental charity dedicated to caring for orphans, founded on 10 February 2014 under Royal Decree No. 14/2000.

Bahjah provides care and assistance to orphans, including financial, emotional, health, educational and social support.

Its goal is not only that an orphan lives… but that they grow up in a safer, more dignified and hopeful environment.

FAQ

Questions about giving to renovate orphans' homes

Where does my donation go?

Your gift goes to the "Building & Renovation" (بناء وترميم) fund of the Omani Bahjah Orphan Society, to support maintaining, renovating and building the homes of the families it serves, according to each case's needs and the assessment of Bahjah's team.

What does renovation include?

It can include repairing deteriorated roofs, restoring cracked walls and preparing essential facilities such as kitchens and bathrooms, as well as building work when needed.

Is the 10-homes campaign still open?

The campaign to renovate ten homes was announced in March 2026. The "Building & Renovation" fund is a permanent donation option; to ask about a specific campaign, you can contact Bahjah directly.

Can I give a small amount?

Yes. You can give whatever you are able to; in its renovation campaign, Bahjah used the phrase "Give, even if only one rial."

How do I donate?

Tap the donate button to go to the official "Building & Renovation" page (in Arabic), choose the quantity and amount, and complete payment through the available channels. The page shows a unit value of "1,000 ر.ع.", which means one Omani rial, so type your amount in rials in the "الكمية" (Quantity) field (for example, 20 = twenty rials), then tap "تبرع الان" (Donate now).

Which payment methods are available?

According to the FAQ page on Bahjah's website: "We accept credit and debit cards through the Bank Muscat SmartPay gateway."

Are there other ways to contribute?

Yes, choose whatever suits you: transfer to Bahjah's bank accounts, text the word "تبرع" to the toll-free number 90021 to donate 1 OMR (Omantel and Ooredoo), or donate through the Bahjah app. Details are in the section below.

How can I contact Bahjah?

Bahjah's team is happy to hear from you: Phone 92877577 – 23289966 · WhatsApp 92877577 · Email bahjah1.omani@gmail.com · Address: Dhofar / Salalah East / 23 July Street / next to Bank Dhofar
